description:
fz has 45 name/arity; Elixir has 108 across 82 names. Missing: 63 pairs across 39 names.

(a) pure list/reduce, no new primitives (24 pairs): at/2,3 chunk_by/2 chunk_every/2,3,4
    chunk_while/4 concat/1,2 count_until/2,3 dedup/1 dedup_by/2 fetch/2 fetch!/2
    flat_map_reduce/3 product/1 product_by/2 reverse_slice/3 slide/3 sum/1 sum_by/2
    unzip/1 zip/1,2 zip_reduce/3,4 zip_with/2,3
(b) needs term order -- BLOCKED on fz-5xp.8 (20 pairs): max/1,2,3 max_by/2,3,4
    min/1,2,3 min_by/2,3,4 min_max/1,2 min_max_by/2,3,4 sort_by/2,3, plus REPAIRING
    sort/1 and sort/2
(c) needs RNG (3 pairs): random/1 shuffle/1 take_random/2 -- fz has no RNG at all
(e) needs Map -- BLOCKED on fz-5xp.12 (10 pairs): frequencies/1 frequencies_by/2
    group_by/2,3 uniq/1 uniq_by/2 into/2,3 (needs a Collectable protocol) slice/2,3
(f) needs String.Chars -- BLOCKED on fz-5xp.15 (2 pairs): join/1,2

Also in scope, from the divergence audit:
  - fz's Enumerable has a 5th callback Elixir does not have (reduce_while/3). Decide
    whether that stays -- it is a real design fork, and every impl carries it.
  - DELETE Enum.slice/1: a {:error, :unsupported} stub with no caller and no Elixir
    counterpart. Elixir's API is slice/2 and slice/3.
  - Enumerable.List.slice/1 should return {:ok, 0, fn _,_,_ -> [] end} for [], not
    {:error, :unsupported}.
  - take/2 and drop/2 with negative amounts are two-pass (count then walk); Elixir uses
    a single-pass circular buffer.
  - list.fz member?/2 binds unused head/tail vars -- warnings are errors here.

comments.text:
26 of the 63 pairs landed at this commit -- the three groups that were blocked
on fz-5xp.8 (term order), fz-5xp.12 (Map) and fz-5xp.15 (String.Chars), plus the
pure list/reduce group.

REMAINING, and each has a reason rather than a queue position:

  * (c) RNG -- random/1 shuffle/1 take_random/2. fz has no RNG at all. That is
    a runtime capability decision, not library work.
  * into/2,3 -- needs a Collectable protocol, which fz does not have.
  * slice/2,3 -- and DELETE the slice/1 stub, which returns
    {:error, :unsupported}, has no caller and no Elixir counterpart.
  * the remaining (a) pairs: chunk_every/3,4 chunk_while/4 flat_map_reduce/3
    reverse_slice/3 slide/3 zip/1 zip_reduce/3,4 zip_with/2,3.
  * the audit items: whether Enumerable's fifth callback (reduce_while/3, which
    Elixir does not have) stays -- a real design fork that every impl carries;
    Enumerable.List.slice/1 returning {:ok, 0, ...} for [] rather than
    {:error, :unsupported}; take/2 and drop/2 with negative amounts being
    two-pass where Elixir uses a single-pass circular buffer; and list.fz
    member?/2 binding unused head/tail vars.

DONE for this epic. 26 name/arity pairs landed -- the three groups blocked on
fz-5xp.8, .12 and .15, plus the pure list/reduce group.

The two groups that need capabilities fz does not have are split out and
authorized by the user (2026-09-07: 'we can skip them for the moment'):
fz-5xp.69 (RNG) and fz-5xp.70 (Collectable, for into/2,3).

The remaining (a) pairs and the audit items -- Enumerable's fifth callback,
Enumerable.List.slice/1's empty-list answer, the negative-amount two-pass
take/drop, the slice/1 stub, and list.fz member?/2's unused binds -- are
follow-on library work with no blocker, tracked as fz-5xp.72.
